Discrepancy or gap: The reissued Form 4-A, which Bidders must use, prints the superseded Proposal Due Date (12 November 2026) although Section 2.1 of the same Addendum substitutes 26 November 2026, and Volume IV says Form wording is not to be altered; no correction method is stated. It also omits the original form's commercial registration number, registered address, contact email/telephone, Power of Attorney reference and date and company seal fields and its numbered paragraphs 1-6, and refers to an acknowledgement 'at paragraph 1' that it does not contain.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-01 Appendix A makes the reissued form the one to use (an Addendum prevails over Volume IV, VOL-I 3.2(a)); ADD-02 does not reissue it. The Proposal Due Date itself is settled at 26 November 2026, 14:00 Riyadh time (ADD-01 2.1; VOL-I 2.6).
Practical impact: Form 4-A is the first Envelope A item (VOL-I 9.1(a)) and an unsigned or improperly executed Form 4-A renders the Proposal non-responsive (VOL-I 9.3). Whether a printed stale date, a hand correction or an omitted field makes the form 'improperly executed' is not stated, so the form cannot be finalised with certainty.
Proposed question (draft): Addendum No. 1, Appendix A (Revised Form 4-A), page 3: (a) The reissued Form 4-A prints the Proposal Due Date as '12 November 2026, 14:00 Riyadh time', whereas Section 2.1 of the same Addendum (page 1) substitutes Thursday 26 November 2026, and Volume IV, page 2, provides that Forms shall be reproduced without alteration to their wording. How are Bidders to correct the printed date? (b) The reissued form does not include the commercial registration number, registered address, contact email and telephone, Power of Attorney reference and date, company seal or numbered paragraphs 1 to 6 of the original Form 4-A (Volume IV, page 3), and Appendix A refers to an acknowledgement 'at paragraph 1' that the reissued form does not contain. Is the reissued form to be submitted as printed, or are any of the omitted fields or paragraphs to be included?
Interim handling: Use the ADD-01 Appendix A form as the baseline and complete its own fields, including the numbers of all Addenda issued; do not merge it with the original form and do not adopt a date-correction method until an Addendum answers or Legal records a decision. Prepare what the original form covered under its independent Volume I obligations (Powers of Attorney 9.1(h) and 9.3, validity 7.1, Bid Bond 6.3-6.4, single point of contact 4.3, single participation 8.2), without treating a blank field as automatic rejection.
Sources (verbatim): ADD-01:AppA/para1 p3: “Form 4-A is reissued below to add the acknowledgement of Addenda at paragraph 1. Bidders shall use this version.”; ADD-01:AppA/proposal-due-date p3: “Proposal Due Date: 12 November 2026, 14:00 Riyadh time”; ADD-01:2.1 p1: “Thursday 26 November 2026”; VOL-IV:cover/para5 p2: “Forms shall be reproduced without alteration to their wording. A Bidder that alters the wording of a Form does so at its own risk.”; VOL-IV:F4-A/power-of-attorney-reference-and-date p3: “Power of Attorney reference and date:”; VOL-I:9.3 p5: “An unsigned or improperly executed Form 4-A shall render the Proposal non-responsive.”

Clause: Form 4-B (field 'Contract value (SAR equivalent)'), with Volume I Clause 6.2
Discrepancy or gap: Form 4-B, which goes in Envelope A, asks for each reference project's contract value in SAR, while VOL-I 6.2 makes any price, rate or other commercial information in Envelope A non-responsive. 'Other commercial information' is not defined and no exception is stated for historical contract values.
Already settled (not re-asked): Nothing settles it. VOL-I 3.2 ranks Volume I above Volume IV, but whether a historical contract value is 'commercial information' (and so whether the two conflict at all) is the open point; no Addendum answer addresses it.
Practical impact: Completing the field risks non-responsiveness under VOL-I 6.2 across every Form 4-B; leaving it blank departs from a form that is to be reproduced unaltered and weakens the reference evidence on which technical capability is assessed (VOL-I 8.5).
Proposed question (draft): Volume IV, Form 4-B, page 4, and Volume I, Clause 6.2, page 3: Form 4-B, which Volume I Clause 9.1(b) places in Envelope A, includes the field 'Contract value (SAR equivalent)'. Clause 6.2 provides that the appearance of any price, rate or other commercial information within Envelope A shall render the Proposal non-responsive. Does the contract value of a reference project entered in Form 4-B constitute 'other commercial information' for the purposes of Clause 6.2, and how is the field to be completed?
Interim handling: Keep the field in Form 4-B as issued and collect the contract values with the reference evidence; do not treat them as exempt, delete the field or move the values to Envelope B. Whether the Envelope A forms show the values stays an open Legal decision, gated before Envelope A is finalised.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-IV:F4-B/contract-value-sar-equivalent p4: “Contract value (SAR equivalent):”; VOL-I:6.2 p3: “The appearance of any price, rate, or other commercial information within Envelope A shall render the Proposal non-responsive.”; VOL-I:9.1 p4: “Envelope A shall contain, in the following order and separated by numbered dividers:”; VOL-I:9.1(b) p4: “(b) Form 4-B — Reference Projects Schedule (one per reference project);”

Discrepancy or gap: VOL-I 10.1 and the Form 4-F note limit Envelope B to Form 4-F and the Financial Model, yet 10.3 requires a model auditor's opinion to accompany the Financial Model and 10.6 a financing-assumptions schedule to be submitted with Form 4-F. Where these two documents go is not stated, and they cannot go in Envelope A (6.2).
Already settled (not re-asked): No Addendum answer addresses it. The Excel format of the Financial Model (10.3) is not in question.
Practical impact: Both documents are required, but placing them in Envelope B appears to breach 10.1 and placing them in Envelope A would put commercial information there (non-responsive, 6.2). Affects Envelope B assembly and the Form 4-F model-auditor and opinion-date fields.
Proposed question (draft): Volume I, Clauses 10.1, 10.3 and 10.6, page 5: Clause 10.1 (and the note to Form 4-F, Volume IV, page 9) states that Envelope B shall contain only Form 4-F and the Financial Model, while Clause 10.3 requires the Financial Model to be accompanied by an opinion from an independent model auditor and Clause 10.6 requires a schedule of the principal financing assumptions to be submitted with Form 4-F. How and where are the model auditor's opinion and the financing assumptions schedule to be submitted?
Interim handling: Prepare both documents in full: the model audit on the Excel model, and the schedule covering tenor, margin and gearing consistent with Form 4-F. Keep both out of Envelope A; the packaging decision stays open with the Bid manager until an Addendum answers or a dated internal decision is recorded with its risk.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-I:10.1 p5: “Envelope B shall contain only (a) Form 4-F (Financial Proposal Schedule) and (b) the Financial Model. No other document shall be placed in Envelope B.”; VOL-I:10.3 p5: “shall be accompanied by an opinion from an independent model auditor addressed to the Authority”; VOL-I:10.6 p5: “The Bidder shall submit with Form 4-F a schedule of the principal financing assumptions underlying the Availability Payment, including the assumed debt tenor, margin and gearing.”; VOL-IV:F4-F/envelope-b-only p9: “This Form and the Financial Model are the only documents to be placed in Envelope B.”

Discrepancy or gap: VOL-I 6.5 calls for one encrypted USB electronic copy per Proposal but does not say how it relates to the two separately sealed envelopes, or how the means of decryption is given to the Authority. A single USB holding both envelopes' content could not go in Envelope A without commercial information (6.2), or in Envelope B without other documents (10.1).
Already settled (not re-asked): Copy quantities are per Proposal, as 6.5 states ('Each Proposal shall be submitted as...'); that is not in question.
Practical impact: Wrong packaging could put commercial information in Envelope A (non-responsive, 6.2) or breach the restricted Envelope B contents (10.1); media the Authority cannot decrypt defeat the electronic copy (the marked original governs if they differ, 6.5).
Proposed question (draft): Volume I, Clause 6.5, page 3: Clause 6.5 requires one searchable electronic copy on encrypted USB media for each Proposal, while Clause 6.2 (page 3) requires two separately sealed envelopes and Clause 10.1 (page 5) restricts the contents of Envelope B. How is the electronic copy to be packaged in relation to Envelopes A and B, and how is the means of decrypting the USB media to be provided to the Authority?
Interim handling: Build the electronic copy as two separable sets (Envelope A and Envelope B content, matching the [ENV] element of Appendix 2) so either arrangement can be adopted late, and never place Envelope B content with Envelope A. Encryption method and key delivery stay open with the Bid manager; quantities remain one original, three hard copies and one electronic copy per Proposal.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-I:6.5 p3: “Each Proposal shall be submitted as one (1) marked original, three (3) hard copies, and one (1) searchable electronic copy on encrypted USB media.”; VOL-I:6.2 p3: “Each Proposal shall be submitted in two separately sealed and clearly marked envelopes: Envelope A (Technical Proposal) and Envelope B (Commercial Proposal).”; VOL-I:10.1 p5: “No other document shall be placed in Envelope B.”

Discrepancy or gap: Declaration 4 (Arabic; owner-confirmed translation: 'all information submitted in this proposal is true and complete ... any incorrect statement leads to the exclusion of the proposal') attaches a consequence, استبعاد العرض, to any incorrect statement in the Proposal. Volume I never uses 'exclusion' as a consequence (it uses rejection, disqualification, non-responsiveness and 'disregarded') and has no clause on incorrect statements, so the meaning and stage of this consequence are not stated; it is not equated with any of them.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-02 Q9 settles that Form 4-C is completed in Arabic with an English translation for convenience only, and VOL-I 9.4 makes the Arabic govern; neither addresses the effect of declaration 4.
Practical impact: Every member signs this declaration for Envelope A (VOL-I 9.1(c), 9.4) and accepts a consequence that cannot be placed in the Volume I evaluation stages; it reaches all information in the Proposal, so any error anywhere carries an undefined risk.
Proposed question (draft): Volume IV, Form 4-C, declaration 4, page 6: Declaration 4 states that any incorrect statement 'يؤدي إلى استبعاد العرض' (translated as 'leads to the exclusion of the proposal'). Volume I does not use the term 'exclusion' and does not otherwise address incorrect statements in a Proposal. What is the effect of 'استبعاد العرض' under Volume I, including the stage of the evaluation in Clause 11.1 (page 5) at which it would apply, and does it correspond to any consequence stated in Volume I?
Interim handling: Sign Form 4-C as issued, in Arabic, without altering the declaration, and record 'exclusion' as its own unresolved consequence category (not mapped to rejection, disqualification or non-responsiveness). Run a documented accuracy check across the whole Proposal before each member signs.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-IV:F4-C/image/decl4 p6: “أن جميع المعلومات المقدمة في هذا العرض صحيحة وكاملة”; VOL-IV:F4-C/image/decl4 p6: “وندرك أن أي بيان غير صحيح يؤدي إلى استبعاد العرض”; VOL-I:9.4 p5: “A translation may be attached for convenience but the Arabic text shall govern.”; VOL-I:11.1 p5: “(i) a responsiveness and mandatory compliance check on a pass or fail basis”

Discrepancy or gap: The reinstated 8.6 requires a certificate 'issued by the competent authority' but does not name that authority, the application route or its lead time, or what the certificate must evidence at the Proposal Due Date for a construction phase that has not started.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-02 9.1-9.2 reinstate the requirement at 35% with non-responsiveness for failure to submit, superseding ADD-01 Section 4 (a later Addendum prevails, VOL-I 3.2(a)); the requirement itself is not in question.
Practical impact: A missing certificate makes the Proposal non-responsive, and its issue depends on a third party with an unknown lead time; about five weeks separate ADD-02 (22 October) from the Proposal Due Date. The minutes (non-binding) record bidders' difficulty obtaining it.
Proposed question (draft): Addendum No. 2, Section 9.1, page 3 (Volume I Clause 8.6 as reinstated): Which body is the 'competent authority' that issues the Local Content Certificate, and what must the certificate evidence at the Proposal Due Date in respect of the local content ratio 'for the construction phase'?
Interim handling: Treat the certificate as a critical-path, non-responsiveness item: identify the likely issuing body, start the application and a local content plan of at least 35% now, and track the lead time. Do not assume that an application receipt or any substitute will be accepted.
Sources (verbatim): ADD-02:9.1 p3: “The Bidder shall submit a Local Content Certificate issued by the competent authority evidencing a local content ratio of not less than thirty-five per cent (35%) for the construction phase. Failure to submit the certificate shall render the Proposal non-responsive.”; ADD-02:9.2 p3: “Section 4.2 of Addendum No. 1 ceases to have effect.”; ADD-01:AppB/item-4-local-content p4: “A Bidder raised difficulty in obtaining a Local Content Certificate within the programme.”

Discrepancy or gap: Volume V is an extract: Schedules 7 (deductions), 9 (indexation), 11 (Project Company defaults) and 12 (termination compensation), the Direct Agreement and the omitted clauses (including those defining Notice to Proceed and Force Majeure Event) are referred to but not issued, yet the Note to Bidders deems any deviation not listed in Form 4-E accepted.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-02 Q12 refers Bidders to 31.2, under which deductions are uncapped; ADD-01 Q6 confirms the payment is availability based. Neither supplies the missing Schedules.
Practical impact: The Availability Payment in Form 4-F and the Financial Model depend on Schedule 9 (index series, base date) and Schedule 7 (deduction levels); termination sums and lender cure rights (Schedules 11-12, Direct Agreement) drive financing terms. Form 4-E cannot list deviations to terms not seen, yet unlisted deviations are deemed accepted.
Proposed question (draft): Volume V, Note to Bidders, page 2: The extract refers to Schedules 7, 9, 11 and 12 and to the Direct Agreement (Clauses 29.2, 31.2, 39.1, 39.5 and 40.1, pages 3-4), none of which has been issued, and states that a deviation not listed in Form 4-E will be taken as accepted. Will the Authority issue these Schedules and the Direct Agreement or, if not, does the deemed acceptance in the Note to Bidders apply only to the clauses reproduced in the extract?
Interim handling: Build the Financial Model on the reproduced terms (60% CPI / 40% fixed indexation per 29.2; uncapped deductions per 31.2) and record the index and deduction inputs as assumptions in the financing-assumptions schedule, not as price conditions (VOL-I 10.5). Legal decides whether to record a reservation on the unseen Schedules in Form 4-E; nothing is assumed about their content.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-V:cover/note-to-bidders p2: “Clause numbering follows the full draft; omitted clauses are not reproduced. A deviation not listed in Form 4-E will be taken as accepted.”; VOL-V:29.2 p3: “The Availability Payment shall be indexed annually in accordance with Schedule 9”; VOL-V:31.2 p3: “the Authority shall deduct from the Availability Payment the amounts calculated under Schedule 7”; VOL-V:39.1 p4: “being the events listed in Schedule 11”; VOL-V:39.5 p4: “the notice and cure period stated in the Direct Agreement”; VOL-V:40.1 p4: “calculated under Schedule 12”

Clause: Section 6, response to question 7 (Volume I Clause 12.1; Volume V Clauses 3.1 and 42.2)
Discrepancy or gap: VOL-I 12.1 runs the concession twenty-five years 'commencing on the Project Commercial Operation Date'; VOL-V 3.1 runs the Agreement twenty-five years 'from the Effective Date'. ADD-02 Q7 answers that the order of precedence at VOL-I 3.2 applies and that no further amendment is considered necessary, without saying which clause applies; neither clause is amended. Open: which clause governs the term (a decision for a person, Legal; no decision recorded); whether VOL-V 3.1 left unlisted in Form 4-E would be 'taken as accepted' under the Volume V Note; and how 'the term' in VOL-V 3.2 and 42.2 is to be read.
Already settled (not re-asked): Only the Authority's response, quoted: ADD-02 Q7 'The Authority notes the question. The order of precedence at Volume I Clause 3.2 applies. The Authority does not consider further amendment necessary at this stage.' Neither VOL-I 12.1 nor VOL-V 3.1 is amended. The response does not say which clause applies: which clause governs is not treated as settled (pending Legal; no decision recorded).
Practical impact: The readings differ by the construction period (36 months from Notice to Proceed, VOL-V 12.1, plus any time from the Effective Date), changing the years of Availability Payment, debt tenor, the year-20 handback reserve trigger and the handback date; the Financial Model and Form 4-E depend on which reading a person adopts (Legal; none adopted).
Proposed question (draft): Addendum No. 2, response to question 7, page 2; Volume V, Clauses 3.1 (page 2) and 42.2 (page 4): Further to the Authority's response that the order of precedence in Volume I Clause 3.2 applies to the concession term, will a Bidder that does not list Volume V Clause 3.1 in Form 4-E be taken, under the Note to Bidders in Volume V, to have accepted a term running from the Effective Date, and is 'the term' in Volume V Clauses 3.2 and 42.2 to be read as the twenty-five (25) year period commencing on PCOD stated in Volume I Clause 12.1 (page 6)?
Interim handling: Pending Legal's decision (no decision recorded): carry both readings in the Financial Model, 25 years of operation from PCOD (VOL-I 12.1) and 25 years from the Effective Date (VOL-V 3.1), and present neither as settled. Legal decides which reading to price, whether to record VOL-V 3.1 in Form 4-E (citing VOL-I 12.1 and ADD-02 Q7), and whether to ask the Authority again, before the VOL-I 5.2 cut-off, which clause applies.
Sources (verbatim): ADD-02:Q7 p2: “The order of precedence at Volume I Clause 3.2 applies. The Authority does not consider further amendment necessary at this stage.”; VOL-I:12.1 p6: “The concession period shall be twenty-five (25) years commencing on the Project Commercial Operation Date”; VOL-V:3.1 p2: “shall continue for a period of twenty-five (25) years from the Effective Date”; VOL-V:42.2 p4: “A handback reserve shall be funded from the start of year twenty (20) of the term”; VOL-V:cover/note-to-bidders p2: “A deviation not listed in Form 4-E will be taken as accepted.”

Discrepancy or gap: 'Dry weather flow' is not defined. If it equals the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day, i.e. 5,000 m³/h), the storm flow to be passed to full treatment (3 x DWF, 15,000 m³/h) is twice the peak hourly design flow of 7,500 m³/h used for the hydraulic profile and the transmission main (VOL-II 4.1, 5.2), so the governing storm design flow is unclear.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-02 Q11 answers the question asked: 'Bidders shall design to the figures stated in Volume II. Volume II Clause 4.2 applies.' That is not re-asked. The Authority does not comment on consistency; that the average daily flow (120,000 m³/day, 5,000 m³/h) and the peak hourly flow (7,500 m³/h) are not contradictory (a peaking factor of 1.5) is an engineering reading for the process engineer to confirm. Q11 did not address row 2-6.4 or define dry weather flow (DWF); VOL-II 4.2 itself asks Bidders to raise flow inconsistencies under VOL-I 5.1.
Practical impact: Sets the hydraulic capacity of the inlet works, treatment streams and channels and possibly of the transmission main and reservoir; a two-fold difference in storm design flow is a major capex and footprint item and bears on meeting Table 2-4 under storm conditions.
Proposed question (draft): Volume II, Table 2-6, row 2-6.4, page 4: How is 'dry weather flow' in row 2-6.4 defined, and what storm flow, in m³/h, is to be passed to full treatment and accommodated by the hydraulic profile under Clause 4.1 (page 3), given that three times a dry weather flow equal to the average daily flow in row 2-6.1 (120,000 m³/day) would exceed the peak hourly flow (design) of 7,500 m³/h in row 2-6.2?
Interim handling: Design to the stated Table 2-6 figures and carry the more onerous reading (3 x average daily flow, 15,000 m³/h, through inlet works and full treatment) as the hydraulic case, with the 7,500 m³/h case costed as a variant. Record the assumption in the design basis; add no qualification to the Proposal.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.4 p4: “Storm flow to be passed to full treatment”; VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.4 p4: “3 x dry weather flow”; VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.1 p3: “Average daily flow | Value: 120,000 | Unit: m³/day”; VOL-II:T2-6/2-6.2 p3: “Peak hourly flow (design) | Value: 7,500 | Unit: m³/h”; VOL-II:4.1 p3: “The hydraulic profile shall accommodate the flows in Table 2-6 without surcharge of any structure and without reliance on pumped bypass.”; ADD-02:Q11 p2: “Bidders shall design to the figures stated in Volume II. Volume II Clause 4.2 applies.”

Discrepancy or gap: The Environmental Permit is not among the RFP Documents, yet it prevails over the Table 2-4 reproduction (VOL-II page 3 preamble) and, by Note 1, sets the limits for any parameter not listed. Bidders cannot see those limits or check the reproduction, and whether the Permit reflects the ADD-02 TN amendment is not stated.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-02 5.1 sets TN at 3 mg/l on the same basis for the RFP Documents (an Addendum prevails, VOL-I 3.2(a)), superseding the original 5 mg/l reading. The minutes' remark that the permit was under review (ADD-01 Appendix B item 5) does not bind (ADD-01 3.2).
Practical impact: Unknown limits for unlisted parameters, and any Permit value stricter than the reproduction, bear on process design (criterion A, 25 marks), the performance risk priced into the Availability Payment and possibly Unavailability Events under VOL-V 31.1(b), which have no cure period. Permit compliance cannot be claimed.
Proposed question (draft): Volume II, Clause 2.4 (page 2) and Table 2-4, Note 1 (page 3): Table 2-4 is reproduced from the Environmental Permit, which is stated to prevail in any discrepancy, and Note 1 applies the Permit's limits to any parameter not listed. The Permit has not been issued with the RFP Documents. Will the Authority issue the Environmental Permit or, failing that, state the limits and bases of assessment it sets for parameters not listed in Table 2-4, and is the Permit consistent with Table 2-4 as amended by Addendum No. 2, Section 5.1 (page 1)?
Interim handling: Design to Table 2-4 as amended (TN 3 mg/l on the 30-day rolling-average basis) and make no claim of Permit compliance, including for the TN amendment. Record unlisted-parameter limits as an open design risk; completing the bid does not depend on receiving the Permit.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-II:2.4 p2: “Table 2-4 is reproduced overleaf from the Environmental Permit issued for the site and is incorporated into this Volume by reference.”; VOL-II:T2-4-heading/para1 p3: “In the event of any discrepancy between this reproduction and the Environmental Permit, the Environmental Permit shall prevail.”; VOL-II:T2-4/note1 p3: “Where a parameter is not listed above, the limit stated in the Environmental Permit shall apply.”; ADD-02:5.1 p1: “the limit for Total Nitrogen (TN) is amended from the value shown to 3 mg/l, assessed on the same basis.”

Clause: Table 2-4 (Residual Chlorine and pH rows), with Clause 3.3
Discrepancy or gap: Residual Chlorine (0.5 - 1.0 mg/l) and pH (6.0 - 9.0) are printed as ranges under a qualifier that 'all values are maxima'. If 0.5 mg/l is a minimum residual at the outlet, ultraviolet-only disinfection and dechlorination, both permitted by VOL-II 3.3, could not comply; if it is not, the lower figures have no stated function.
Already settled (not re-asked): ADD-01 Q1 settles that no process train is mandated but does not address disinfection residuals. The printed qualifier and each row's basis of assessment are as read and confirmed; nothing settles the ranges.
Practical impact: Determines whether a chlorine dosing and residual-control system is required at the outlet whatever disinfection method is chosen, and how continuously monitored failures arise (VOL-II 2.5; VOL-V 31.1(b), no cure period).
Proposed question (draft): Volume II, Table 2-4 and Clause 3.3, page 3: Table 2-4 states that all values are maxima, but gives Residual Chlorine as 0.5 - 1.0 mg/l and pH as 6.0 - 9.0, each assessed 'Continuous at outlet'. Are the lower values (0.5 mg/l Residual Chlorine and pH 6.0) minimum limits and, if a minimum chlorine residual applies, does it apply where disinfection is by ultraviolet irradiation alone or by chlorination with dechlorination as permitted by Clause 3.3?
Interim handling: Treat both ranges as two-sided limits for design and provide the ability to hold a 0.5 - 1.0 mg/l chlorine residual at the outlet whatever primary disinfection is selected; keep each parameter's printed basis of assessment.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-II:T2-4 p3: “(all values are maxima; compliance assessed as a 30-day rolling average unless stated)”; VOL-II:T2-4/ResidualChlorine p3: “Limit: 0.5 - 1.0 | Basis of assessment: Continuous at outlet”; VOL-II:T2-4/pH p3: “Limit: 6.0 - 9.0 | Basis of assessment: Continuous at outlet”; VOL-II:3.3 p3: “Disinfection shall be by chlorination with provision for dechlorination, or by ultraviolet irradiation with a validated dose, or by a combination.”

Will the Authority issue Volume III or, failing that, state the location and ground level of the delivery point shown on Drawing 03-C-114 and the location of the two designated tie-in points referred to in Clause 1.3?
Interim handling: Design and price the main on the stated parameters (about 18 km, minimum DN1200, maximum 2.0 m/s, 15 m residual head) with the delivery point, route and tie-in locations as labelled assumptions and a cost allowance; completing the bid does not depend on receiving Volume III.
Sources (verbatim): VOL-I:3.1 p2: “Volume III (Drawings)”; VOL-II:5.1 p4: “between the Facility outlet chamber and the delivery point shown on Drawing 03-C-114”; VOL-II:5.2 p4: “a minimum residual head of 15 m at the delivery point”; VOL-II:1.3 p2: “at the two designated tie-in points”; VOL-I:3.4 p3: “No claim arising from an alleged omission shall be entertained after the Proposal Due Date.”

Discrepancy or gap: The Bid Bond runs 180 days from the Proposal Due Date (to about 25 May 2027) and must be extended only when Proposal validity is extended, but VOL-I 12.2 lets the Authority call it if Financial Close is missed, up to 270 days after the Preferred Bidder Notification (as late as about January 2028 if notification comes at the end of the 150-day validity). Practical impact: Determines the expiry date and extension commitment the issuing bank must give, and its cost, and the Preferred Bidder's exposure to a call at Financial Close; a fixed-expiry bank instrument must be drafted to match.
